metaDescription: Seven cordless chainsaws at or under $100 compared on bar length, motor type, battery and oiling, with an honest line between pruning and real cutting.
expertTake: The Seesii Flagship 8 inch is the best pick under this cap because it pairs a brushless motor with an 8 inch bar and two 4000 mAh packs, which is the most cutting capacity you can buy at this level. The Greenworks 24V 6 inch is the value pick for a buyer who wants a known brand and a battery that fits other tools. Anyone planning to fell trees or cut firewood should skip this price class and buy a full-size saw.
introParagraphs: At this price a cordless chainsaw is really a pruning saw with a chain. It cuts branches, trims small trees and clears storm debris, and it does it without fuel mixing or a pull cord.

That limit decides what to buy. Bar length, motor type, battery capacity and oiling system matter more than the wattage claims on the box, and a few safety details are worth checking before the first cut. This guide explains how to read them.

products.name: SEESII Flagship 8 inch cordless mini chainsaw, brushless
products.description:
The Seesii Flagship is the most capable pruning saw in this price class. It combines a brushless motor with an 8 inch bar, which gives more reach than the 6 inch minis and handles branches roughly the thickness of a forearm. Brushless motors run cooler and use battery energy more efficiently than brushed ones, so the 4000 mAh packs last longer than their size suggests.

Two batteries are included, and the seller quotes 150 or more cuts per charge pair. Treat that as a best-case number on small softwood branches, because dense hardwood drains a pack much faster. The 1000W figure is a rating, not a measured output, so do not compare it directly with a full-size saw. Against the Greenworks 6 inch, it gives you a larger bar and more battery, while the Greenworks gives you a brand with replacement packs on the shelf.

As with every saw here, keep the oil tank filled, check chain tension before each session and sharpen or replace the chain when it starts producing dust instead of chips. Use two hands whenever the bar allows, and do not cut above shoulder height.
products.bestFor: Homeowners who prune thick branches and want the most bar and battery under the cap.
pros: Brushless motor runs cooler and lasts longer
Handheld size suits ladders and tight spots
cons: Rated wattage is not comparable to full-size saws
Quoted cut counts assume easy wood
Unbranded support is thinner than big names

products.name: Greenworks 24V 6 inch brushless mini chainsaw, 2.0Ah
products.description:
The Greenworks is the pick for anyone who values a familiar brand and a shared battery. The 24V pack fits a large family of Greenworks tools, so it can be the starting point of a yard-tool set rather than a one-off purchase. A brushless motor and a 6 inch bar make it a capable branch and small-log cutter.

It weighs 3.4 pounds with the battery, which is light enough for one-handed overhead trimming that you should still do carefully. A security lock stops accidental starts, a useful detail for a tool marketed to seniors and occasional users. The 2.0Ah pack stores 48 watt hours, which is modest, so plan on trimming sessions of a few dozen cuts rather than an afternoon of work.

Compared with the Seesii Flagship, you get a smaller bar and battery but better odds of finding a replacement pack in future. Keep the chain tight, oil it before each use and store the battery partly charged in a dry place.
products.bestFor: Buyers who want a mainstream brand and a battery that fits other tools.
pros: Brushless motor in a light body
Brand makes replacement parts easier to find
cons: Less cutting capacity than the Seesii

products.name: DOOYUTOOL 10 inch brushless chainsaw for DEWALT 20V MAX
products.description:
This saw is built around a simple idea: use the DeWalt 20V MAX batteries you already own. The bare saw takes standard packs, and this listing includes a 4.0Ah battery, so there is a cutting tool in the box. A 10 inch bar is the longest in this guide and brings it into light limbing territory.

A brushless motor and a self-oiling system with a see-through tank handle the two jobs that decide chain life: efficient power and steady lubrication. The oil window lets you see when the reservoir is low before the chain runs dry. Be aware that this is a third-party tool that uses DeWalt batteries, not a DeWalt product, so warranty and support come from the seller.

Compared with the Seesii Flagship, it has a longer bar but depends on a battery platform, and a 20V pack that is already in your garage costs you nothing. Keep an eye on chain tension, because new chains stretch during the first few uses.
products.bestFor: Owners of DeWalt 20V MAX batteries who want a longer-bar saw.
pros: 10 inch bar is the longest in this guide
See-through oil tank shows the level
Brushless motor with a battery included
cons: Depends on a battery platform you own

products.name: Tietoc 6 inch mini electric chainsaw, 880W, auto oiler
products.description:
The Tietoc is a basic 6 inch saw that leads with its automatic chain lubrication. You pour bar oil into the reservoir and the saw feeds it to the chain as it runs, which keeps friction down and lengthens chain life. A manganese steel chain is a standard choice at this tier.

At 3.3 pounds it is light enough to use one-handed on small branches, though a two-handed grip is safer when the angle allows. The 880 watt figure is a rating rather than a measured output, and it should be read as a pruning-saw spec. Compared with the Teeanees, it is heavier but similar in power, and compared with the Seesii Flagship, it lacks brushless efficiency.

This is the machine for light yard work. Keep the reservoir topped up, clean the bar groove and replace the chain when cuts get slow.
products.bestFor: Casual gardeners who want an inexpensive saw with automatic oiling.

products.name: TEEANEES 6 inch mini chainsaw, 21V, 3 chains included
products.description:
The Teeanees is the lightest saw here at 1.88 pounds, which is a real advantage for overhead pruning where fatigue sets in quickly. It runs an 880 watt copper motor at 6800 RPM and quotes a chain speed of 28.6 feet per second, a typical figure for a mini saw.

Three chains are included, which is useful because a spare lets you swap and sharpen instead of stopping the work. A built-in automatic oiler reduces friction, as on the Tietoc. A low weight comes from a small battery and body, so the run time is the compromise, and the 21V pack is not a shared platform.

Compared with the Greenworks, it gives up the brand and the brushless motor, but the weight and the extra chains make it an easy tool to live with. Keep a spare battery charged for larger jobs.
products.bestFor: Users who prune overhead or have limited grip strength and want the lightest saw.

products.name: CEEPUY 6 inch mini chainsaw, 880W, two batteries
products.description:
The Ceepuy is a 6 inch mini saw with two batteries, an automatic oiling system and a security lock that prevents an accidental start. It quotes the same 880 watt and 28.6 foot per second figures as other minis, so the differences are in the details.

The slim body is meant for one-handed operation in tight spaces, and the oil system accepts common bar oil. With two batteries you can swap packs and keep working, which beats a single battery at the same price. The lock switch is a sensible safety touch on a tool that many beginners buy.

Compared with the Tietoc, it adds a second battery and a lock. Compared with the Seesii Flagship, it is smaller and brushed-class. Use bar oil, keep the chain sharp and treat it as a branch-trimmer.
products.bestFor: Beginners who want a lock and a spare battery in a basic 6 inch saw.
cons: Same small bar as other minis
Rated wattage is not measured output

products.name: Seesii 6 inch mini chainsaw, 900W, two 21V batteries
products.description:
The base Seesii is a light 6 inch saw at 2.7 pounds with two 21V 2000 mAh batteries and a precision-hardened chain. The seller describes it as easy to use one-handed, which fits its weight, and quotes 80 to 100 cuts per charge on small stock.

That quoted figure is a best-case result on thin, soft branches, and thicker green wood drains packs much faster. Next to the Flagship, it has a smaller bar, smaller batteries and no brushless motor, so you are paying for the simplest version of the idea. Compared with the Teeanees, it is slightly heavier but offers a second battery.

It makes sense for a household that needs to trim a few bushes and branches each season. Fill the oil reservoir, keep the chain tight, and replace the chain as soon as cuts turn to dust.
products.bestFor: Occasional pruners who want the simplest saw with a spare battery.
pros: Easy one-handed handling for small cuts

buyingCriteria.criterion: Bar length and what it cuts
buyingCriteria.explanation: A 6 inch bar cuts branches up to about that diameter, an 8 inch bar like the Seesii Flagship's reaches thicker limbs, and a 10 inch bar like the DOOYUTOOL's moves into light limbing. Buyers often assume a longer bar means a stronger saw, but the motor and battery decide whether the bar can be used. Match the bar to the wood you actually cut.

Brushless motors run cooler, last longer and make better use of the battery. The Seesii Flagship, Greenworks and DOOYUTOOL list them, while the basic minis do not. At this price the difference is felt in run time more than raw power.

A 2000 mAh pack, as in the base Seesii, stores far less energy than the 4000 mAh packs in the Flagship. A shared platform, such as Greenworks 24V or DeWalt 20V MAX, lets you reuse batteries across tools. Always check whether a battery is included.
880W, 900W and 1000W figures are ratings, and unbranded makers do not use a common test. Do not compare them with a full-size saw. Judge the saw by bar length, motor type and battery.

A saw that runs dry burns its chain and bar. Automatic oilers, as on the Tietoc and Teeanees, help, but you still need to fill the reservoir. Check the oil window and sharpen or replace the chain when it produces dust.

A mini saw is a pruning tool, not a felling saw. Look for a lock switch, such as the Greenworks and Ceepuy have, and use two hands when you can. Never cut above shoulder height or from an unstable ladder.

specDecoder.meaning: A claimed motor power that is not measured under a common test. It is best treated as a rough class label.
specDecoder.watchFor: The Seesii Flagship and DOOYUTOOL claim 1000W while others claim 880W.

specDecoder.meaning: How fast the chain moves. Faster chains cut cleaner at the same power.
specDecoder.watchFor: The Teeanees and Ceepuy quote 28.6 ft/s.

specDecoder.meaning: A measure of stored charge. Compare it at the same voltage.
specDecoder.watchFor: The Flagship uses 4000 mAh packs against 2000 mAh in the base Seesii.

specDecoder.meaning: An electronically commutated motor with no brushes to wear. It is efficient and runs cooler.
specDecoder.watchFor: Listed on the Flagship, Greenworks and DOOYUTOOL.

specDecoder.meaning: A reservoir that feeds bar oil to the chain as it runs. You still need to fill it.
specDecoder.watchFor: The Tietoc, Teeanees and Ceepuy list it.

howWeEvaluated.title: Cutting capacity
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared bar length and motor type from the spec sheet. The 10 inch DOOYUTOOL and 8 inch Seesii Flagship sit above the 6 inch group.

howWeEvaluated.title: Battery and runtime
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared pack size and platform, from 2000 mAh in the base Seesii to 4000 mAh in the Flagship. Shared platforms earn extra credit.

howWeEvaluated.title: Safety features
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked for lock switches and guards. The Greenworks and Ceepuy list a security lock.

howWeEvaluated.title: Care and oiling
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared oiling systems, from auto oilers to a see-through tank. Chain spares, like the Teeanees' three chains, count.

howWeEvaluated.title: Cap check
howWeEvaluated.description: We kept only listings at or under the $100 cap on the day this guide was updated. Prices move, so recheck before buying. Near-identical listings were merged.

cards.label: Brushless
cards.text: The Seesii Flagship, Greenworks and DOOYUTOOL run cooler and make better use of the pack. They cost a little more.

cards.label: Brushed
cards.text: The Tietoc, Teeanees, Ceepuy and base Seesii are cheaper. They draw more from the battery and wear out sooner.

howToChoose.note: Pick brushless if you will use the saw often; pick brushed for occasional trimming.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: A longer bar, a brushless motor and a spare battery, plus a sharp chain. Expect to cut limbs, not trunks.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The DOOYUTOOL 10 inch and SEESII Flagship 8 inch fit best. The 6 inch minis suit smaller twigs only.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You fell trees, cut firewood or work for hours. A full-size cordless saw is the right tool, not one of these.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You trim a few branches a year. The TEEANEES or Tietoc is enough.

maintenance.why: A dry chain burns quickly. Use bar oil, not motor oil.
A loose chain can derail and a tight one strains the motor. New chains stretch early.
A dull chain forces the saw and drains the battery.
Sawdust blocks the oil path. A thin tool clears it.
Lithium cells age faster when full or empty. Keep it cool and dry.

faq.a: No. A 6 to 10 inch bar and a small battery are suited to branches and small logs. Felling needs a full-size saw and training.

faq.q: Why are the watt ratings so high?
faq.a: They are ratings, not measured outputs, and unbranded makers use no common test. Compare bar length, motor type and battery instead. The $100 cap reflects listing prices when this guide was updated.

faq.q: Is a brushless motor worth it?
faq.a: Yes if you cut regularly. It runs cooler and makes better use of the battery. For occasional use, a brushed saw is fine.

faq.q: Can I use these saws one-handed?
faq.a: They are designed for it, but two hands are safer when you can. Never use one on an unstable ladder.

faq.q: How long do the batteries last?
faq.a: Quoted cut counts assume easy wood. Hard or green wood drains packs in a fraction of that. Carry a spare.
Bar and chain oil. Motor oil is too thin or too thick. Check the reservoir before every session.
